metadata.title: GEEK Protocol — Kaspa PSKT transaction coordination
metadata.schema: correctIndex is zero-based; options contains four distinct strings
metadata.reviewNotice: Pinned implementation snapshot only, not a universal wallet or hardware-device compatibility claim. The source contains TODOs, including v1 ComputeBudget support in unsigned_tx; a covenant-format gate does not establish end-to-end support. No signing, key custody, on-chain transfer, deployment, or independent security review is performed by this content change. Advanced transaction-coordination items remain outside the introductory Study filter. Difficulty remains provisional; review is internal.
metadata.attribution: GEEK Protocol original questions based on pinned Rusty Kaspa source; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What workflow is a Partially Signed Kaspa Transaction (PSKT) designed to support?
options: Participants exchanging incomplete transaction data and adding signatures in stages
Asking miners to store the private keys needed for later signatures
Replacing all transaction inputs with public addresses alone
Treating an unsigned payment request as an accepted on-chain payment
questions.funFact: PSKT carries the information needed for coordinated transaction preparation and signing. The format supports cooperation without requiring participants to reveal their private keys.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which transport primitive does Rusty Kaspa's PSKT crate recommend for exchanging a collection of partially signed transactions?
options: One raw transaction with a signature slot for every future transaction
Bundle, which carries multiple PSKT records in one exchange payload
A block-template request carrying all unsigned payments
A node UTXO snapshot used as the final signed transaction
questions.funFact: A wallet operation may require multiple transactions. The crate identifies Bundle as their serialization and transport container; one PSKT represents one transaction.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which role in Rusty Kaspa's PSKT workflow assembles the transaction by adding inputs and outputs?
options: Combiner
Finalizer
Constructor
Signer
questions.funFact: The Constructor assembles inputs and outputs. The separate signing and extraction stages serve different responsibilities.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: In Rusty Kaspa's PSKT Updater, what does set_sequence(n, input_index) update?
options: The sequence values of every input at once
The transaction's global fallback lock time
The minimum required timestamp of the selected input
The sequence value of the selected transaction input
questions.funFact: set_sequence selects an input and sets its sequence metadata. An invalid input index returns an out-of-bounds error.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How does Bundle::merge differ from combining compatible partial records for one transaction in Rusty Kaspa's PSKT crate?
options: Bundle::merge appends transaction records; PSKT combination merges their corresponding metadata
It merges signatures into one shared PSKT and removes the separate transaction records
It validates and broadcasts each appended transaction
It sorts records by fee and retains only the highest-fee transaction
questions.funFact: The Bundle merge loop appends its incoming records. PSKT combination separately merges global, input and output information, subject to compatibility checks.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: How does Rusty Kaspa's PSKT PartialSigs type associate a collected signature with its signer?
options: It maps an input index to one completed unlocking script
It maps a public key to its signature
It maps an output index to the UTXO entry being spent
It maps signature bytes to a master-key fingerprint
questions.funFact: PartialSigs is a map keyed by public key. A signature entry can use the ECDSA or Schnorr representation defined by the crate.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Why does Rusty Kaspa's PSKT Global structure contain both version and tx_version?
options: version is the underlying transaction version; tx_version is the PSKT format version
One selects address encoding; the other selects a signature algorithm
One identifies the PSKT format version; the other identifies the transaction version being built
One selects the network; the other identifies the node RPC revision
questions.funFact: The exchange format and the underlying transaction have distinct version fields. Combining global records checks agreement on each separately.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Two PSKT input records refer to different spent outpoints. How does Rusty Kaspa's input combiner handle them?
options: It merges them whenever the same public key signed both
It automatically turns the two records into separate transaction inputs
It retains whichever record has a newer UTXO DAA score
It rejects the mismatch instead of treating them as one input
questions.funFact: The input combiner checks both the previous transaction ID and the spent output index. A mismatch in either identifies different spent outputs.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Two PSKT records have matching output amounts but different output locking scripts. What does Rusty Kaspa's output combiner do?
options: It rejects them with a script-public-key mismatch
It retains the left script whenever the amounts agree
It accepts either script when both records lack a redeem script
It selects the script belonging to the record with more signatures
questions.funFact: The output combiner requires matching amounts and locking scripts. Agreeing on the quantity alone does not establish agreement on where it can be spent.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: When Rusty Kaspa's PSKT global combiner merges modification flags, what happens if one record disallows adding inputs?
options: The combined flag is true if either input record permits modification
The combined inputs_modifiable flag is false
The combined flag always keeps the left record's value
The merge always fails when the two flags differ
questions.funFact: The combiner uses logical AND for the modification flags. A false flag on either side therefore remains false in the combined metadata.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: A Rusty Kaspa PSKT has input min_time values of 1,000 and 2,000, with fallback_lock_time of 500. Which lock time does determine_lock_time choose?
options: 500, because fallback always overrides the inputs
1,000, the smallest input requirement
2,000, the greatest input requirement
3,500, the sum of every supplied time
questions.funFact: The helper chooses the maximum input min_time. It uses the global fallback when no input specifies a required time, and zero if neither supplies one.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What happens when payload(Some(...)) is called on PSKT format Version::Zero in Rusty Kaspa's constructor?
options: It silently drops the payload and returns a successful result
It accepts the payload whenever the underlying transaction has version 1
It automatically upgrades the PSKT format before storing the payload
It returns an error because a payload requires PSKT version 1 or higher
questions.funFact: The constructor enforces the PSKT format gate before assigning a nonempty optional payload. This is a format check, not a claim of network acceptance.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Under Rusty Kaspa's PSKT constructor, what version conditions are required when adding an output with a covenant binding?
options: PSKT format version at least Two and transaction version at least TX_VERSION_TOCCATA
PSKT format version at least One and transaction version at least TX_VERSION_TOCCATA
PSKT format version at least Two, regardless of the transaction version
Any PSKT format version if its outputs carry enough KAS
questions.funFact: The output constructor rejects covenant bindings if either version requirement is missing. This guard does not establish that every later signing path supports all transaction features.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: A Rusty Kaspa PSKT has three inputs, but its finalization callback returns two script byte vectors. What happens?
options: The missing third vector is filled with an empty placeholder
Finalization returns WrongFinalizedSigsCount
The third input is removed before finalization completes
The second returned vector is reused for the third input
questions.funFact: The finalizer requires one final script byte vector per input. This cardinality check is separate from later execution of the spending scripts.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Even with the right number of input script vectors, which callback result does Rusty Kaspa's PSKT finalizer reject?
options: An input with no BIP32 derivation metadata
An input whose sequence field was initially omitted
An empty final script vector for an input
An input with no separately supplied redeem script
questions.funFact: The finalizer reports EmptySignature for an empty script vector. A nonempty vector passing this check still needs the applicable script-validation step.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which additional check does extract_tx perform beyond extract_tx_unchecked in Rusty Kaspa's PSKT code?
options: It only calculates transaction mass, without running the scripts
It only checks that the serialized bundle text starts with the PSKB prefix
It submits the transaction and waits for a node acceptance response
It executes the populated input spending scripts with the script engine
questions.funFact: Checked extraction invokes the transaction script engine for populated inputs. This local check does not broadcast the transaction or prove that the network has accepted it.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which prefix mapping distinguishes single-record and bundle hexadecimal serialization in Rusty Kaspa's PSKT crate?
options: PSKT for a single record; PSKB for a bundle
PSKB for a single record; PSKT for a bundle
PSKT for both single records and bundles
PSKB for both single records and bundles
questions.funFact: PSKT::to_hex uses the PSKT marker, while Bundle::serialize uses PSKB. Their parsers expect the corresponding marker before decoding the data.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Does Rusty Kaspa's PSKB hexadecimal serialization encrypt the transaction details it contains?
options: Yes; the serializer encrypts JSON with the recipient public key
No; it hex-encodes serialized JSON rather than encrypting it
Only signature bytes are encrypted; transaction amounts remain plaintext
It encrypts unsigned records but exposes finalized records
questions.funFact: Encoding changes representation, not confidentiality. The serializer applies hex encoding to JSON and adds a marker; it does not apply an encryption scheme.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: Which signature-hash type does Input::default select in Rusty Kaspa's PSKT implementation?
options: SIG_HASH_NONE
SIG_HASH_SINGLE
SIG_HASH_ALL
ANYONECANPAY without a base mode
questions.funFact: The default input record explicitly sets SIG_HASH_ALL. An integration must inspect the actual per-input mode rather than infer a signature policy from the PSKT label.
questions.attribution: GEEK Protocol original question based on the cited Rusty Kaspa revision; source prose and code not imported.

questions.prompt: What causes Rusty Kaspa's PSKT Finalizer::extractor transition to return TxNotFinalized?
options: The per-input partial_sigs maps are empty
The output count is zero
The inputs_modifiable and outputs_modifiable flags are false
The global finalized transaction ID is absent
questions.funFact: The role transition checks whether global.id is present. Script validity is addressed separately by checked extraction, so this marker alone is not proof of acceptance.
